Subject: Retention evidence for telemetry + ask on 12mo exception

Hi Markus / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. As we close security review with our legal team, we have one remaining ask: can Redwood provide evidence that telemetry/diagnostic session logs (debug traces, client-side protobufs, and aggregated latency traces) can be retained for 12 months for our tenant only, under a contract carve-out? Our SOC 2 auditor is asking for: (1) controls evidence for retention and deletion, (2) sample proof-of-delete artifacts, and (3) how forensic exports are generated for customer-specific holds.

I've attached a short excerpt from our contract showing the clause (brightline_request_excerpt.pdf). We also flagged SIG/CAIQ questions around storage segmentation and pseudonymization. Can you confirm what artifacts you can provide and an estimated turnaround?

Appreciate it — Samir

Attachments: brightline_request_excerpt.pdf (pdf)

Samir — thanks for the note and the excerpt. Looping in Irene from Security & Compliance and Ben from Customer Success so we can assemble an evidence package and propose a defensible control set for a tenant-specific 12-month retention carve-out.

From: irene.choi@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Retention evidence for telemetry + ask on 12mo exception

Hi Samir / Markus / Ben,

Thanks — happy to get this assembled. Below is a concise plan and the artifacts we can provide. High-level: we support tenant-scoped retention policy overrides for diagnostic/telemetry buckets on Dedicated and Private modes. For Hosted tenants we offer a documented exception path with compensating controls (access restrictions, dedicated bucket, timeboxed SLA).

Requested deliverables (we can produce these within 5 business days after confirmation):
- Retention controls summary (retention_controls_summary.pdf) — describes policy enforcement points, TTL mechanics, and owner approvals.
- SOC 2 artifact index (redwood_soc2_artifacts_index.csv) — examples of control evidence (policy docs, change audit entries, deletion job logs, monitoring alerts).
- SIG/CAIQ response packet (sig_response_packet.xlsx) — answers for the specific CAIQ questions you flagged (storage segmentation, key management, logical separation).
- Forensics export instructions (forensics_export_instructions.md) — step-by-step exported artifact format (CSV/ndjson), redaction/pseudonymization options, and download hashes.
- Sample proof-of-delete package — we will produce a time-stamped deletion job log and object-level tombstone manifest for a small sample set (will include hashes).

Notes on technical approach for a tenant carve-out:
1) Segmented retention: we can place telemetry in a dedicated S3-compatible bucket per tenant (or logical prefix) with a lifecycle TTL controlled by a tagged retention policy.
2) Access controls: RBAC for the bucket, KMS keys scoped to the artifact, and limited principal list (Redwood SOC team + Brightline delegated principals via cross-account role).
3) Pseudonymization: before long-term retention, PII fields can be pseudonymized; raw traces can be archived in an encrypted, access-limited bucket and only decrypted for approved forensic requests.
4) Proof-of-delete: we create an immutable deletion manifest that includes object paths, deletion timestamps, and SHA256 hashes; we can provide signed manifests as evidence.

Attached: retention_controls_summary.pdf, redwood_soc2_artifacts_index.csv, sig_response_packet.xlsx, forensics_export_instructions.md

If Brightline needs a legally-signed attestation, we can escalate to Legal for an addendum. Otherwise, the artifacts above are typical evidence packages we provide to auditors. Happy to hop on a quick call — I have availability Thursday.

Irene Choi
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachments: retention_controls_summary.pdf (pdf), redwood_soc2_artifacts_index.csv (csv), sig_response_packet.xlsx (xlsx), forensics_export_instructions.md (text)
